questions.q: In Mayan architecture, what is the name of the steep, stepped pyramid found in Tikal that served as a funerary monument for Hasaw Cha'an Kawil?
o: Temple I (Temple of the Great Jaguar)
questions.n: This iconic limestone structure rises 47 meters and houses the tomb of one of Tikal's greatest rulers.

questions.q: What is the term for the 'false arch' used by the Mayans, created by offsetting successive courses of stone until they meet at the top?
questions.n: This structural technique involves cantilevering stone layers until the gap is narrow enough to be bridged by a capstone.

questions.q: Which city is home to the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, connected by the Avenue of the Dead?
questions.n: Meaning 'City of the Gods,' this site features some of the largest pyramidal structures in the pre-Columbian Americas.

questions.q: What is the name of the 'Ball Court' used for the ritual game played across Mesoamerica?
questions.n: These I-shaped courts were used for ritualistic games involving a solid rubber ball and stone rings.

questions.q: What is the characteristic architectural style of Teotihuacán, consisting of a slope and a vertical panel?
questions.n: This profile consists of an inward-sloping surface (talud) topped by a rectangular panel (tablero).

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Father of Modern Skyscrapers' and famously stated, 'Form Follows Function'?
questions.n: Sullivan's philosophy and use of steel frames were fundamental to the birth of the modern tall building.

questions.q: Which building in Chicago is considered the first skyscraper to use a complete steel frame to support its weight?
questions.n: Designed by William Le Baron Jenney, it utilized a metal skeleton to allow for greater height and more windows.

questions.q: The Wainwright Building in St. Louis is a masterpiece of which architect?
questions.n: The Wainwright is considered one of the first skyscrapers to successfully express its verticality as a design aesthetic.

questions.q: What is the name of the wide, three-part window (fixed center, operable sides) that became a hallmark of Chicago School buildings?
questions.n: This design allowed for massive daylighting through the center pane while still providing ventilation through the sides.

questions.q: Which architect designed the Flatiron Building in New York, known for its distinct triangular plan?
questions.n: Burnham utilized a Beaux-Arts design for this iconic building on a wedge-shaped lot.

questions.q: Who wrote the influential book 'Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture' and designed the Vanna Venturi House?
questions.n: Venturi challenged Modernist simplicity, famously declaring 'Less is a bore.'

questions.q: Which architect designed the AT&T Building (now 550 Madison Ave) with its famous 'Chippendale' pediment?
questions.n: The building's broken pediment was a shocking departure from the flat roofs of the International Style.

questions.q: The Portland Building, with its bold colors and oversized decorative elements, was designed by whom?
questions.n: This building is considered one of the first major examples of Postmodernism applied to a large civic structure.

questions.q: What is the term coined by Venturi for a building where the form and function are ignored in favor of a decorated 'billboard' façade?
questions.n: This refers to a simple functional box with an elaborate front that communicates its purpose through signs or ornament.

questions.q: Who is the Italian architect known for the Teatro del Mondo and the San Cataldo Cemetery, often associated with Neo-Rationalism/Post-Modernism?
questions.n: Rossi's work focused on primary forms and the collective memory of the city.

questions.q: Who designed the Manila Polo Club and the Forbes Park Pavilion, often emphasizing horizontal lines and tropical ventilation?
questions.n: Antonio is a National Artist known for his elegant Art Deco and tropical modern residences and clubs.

questions.q: Which architect is responsible for the Ramon Magsaysay Center on Roxas Boulevard, a pioneer in the use of pre-stressed concrete?
questions.n: Luz, in collaboration with Pietro Belluschi, designed this building with its distinct structural expression.

questions.q: Who designed the Insular Life Building in Makati, known for the large mosaic on its facade?
questions.n: Concio’s design for Insular Life was a landmark in Makati's early development as a business district.

questions.q: The University of the Philippines Main Library (Gonzalez Hall) was designed by which National Artist?
questions.n: Nakpil designed several key buildings in UP Diliman, including the library and the Carillon tower.

questions.q: Who designed the Iglesia Ni Cristo (INC) Central Temple and developed the distinct 'Spire-heavy' Neo-Gothic Filipino style for INC?
questions.n: Santos-Viola's work created the recognizable and consistent aesthetic for the Iglesia Ni Cristo across the country.

questions.q: What do you call the massive coral stone blocks or adobe blocks used to build the walls of the Bahay na Bato or colonial churches?
questions.n: Sillar blocks were essential for the heavy ground floors of the Bahay na Bato to withstand earthquakes.

questions.q: What is the term for the 'earthquake-proof' Baroque style found in the Philippines, characterized by massive side buttresses?
questions.n: This style adapted European Baroque to the local environment by lowering heights and thickening walls/buttresses.

questions.q: Which historic Philippine city is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its exceptionally preserved Spanish colonial architecture?
questions.n: Vigan is the best-preserved example of a planned Spanish colonial town in Asia.

questions.q: What is the name of the mortar made from lime, sand, and sometimes egg whites used in colonial construction?
questions.n: Argamasa is the traditional lime mortar that has proven to be incredibly durable over centuries.

questions.q: In the Bahay na Bato, what is the 'Media Agua'?
o: A protective secondary roof or awning over a window
questions.n: Media aguas were critical for protecting capiz windows from direct sunlight and heavy rain.
